collection.name: Core consciousness-theory research-profile enrichments
collection.purpose: Deepen high-centrality foundational records whose original entries had citations and summaries but lacked explicit claim boundaries, evidence limitations, and open research questions needed for defensible semantic comparison.
collection.selection_policy: This first tranche prioritizes major scientific theory families and shared explananda that recur throughout consciousness research. It does not rank or endorse them.
collection.identity_policy: Enrichments may not change record identity, name, kind, domain, tradition, proponents, status, summary, or original citations. New evidence may only be appended with an exact locator.
collection.synthesis_policy: No relation among records is asserted. Profiles remain provisional collection objects pending specialist review.

profiles.scope: Cognitive architecture of conscious access and the broad availability of selected information.
profiles.boundary_note: GWT is a functional cognitive architecture. It should not be treated as identical to the later neuronal ignition claims of GNWT, nor as a complete theory of phenomenal character.

claim_scope.target: How selected information becomes globally available to otherwise specialized processors.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A unique neural implementation, that global availability is sufficient for phenomenality, or that every conscious content is reportable.

basis: A broad family of limited-capacity access, working-memory, report, and flexible-control phenomena is consistent with global availability.
The architecture generated explicit computational and neuronal descendants that can be tested more narrowly.
limitations: Many behavioral signatures are compatible with attention, working memory, or executive control without uniquely identifying a global workspace.
Functional descriptions underdetermine both the physical implementation and the relation to subjective experience.
evidence_profile.independence: The retained review compares GWT with other theory families; framework-specific evidence is distributed across heterogeneous paradigms.

open_questions: Which forms of availability are necessary rather than merely correlated with conscious access?
Can global access be operationalized independently of overt report and executive demand?
Which implementations count as the same workspace architecture across biological and artificial systems?

profiles.scope: Neuronal mechanisms proposed to support conscious access through nonlinear ignition and widespread broadcasting.
profiles.boundary_note: GNWT has changed across formulations. Frontoparietal ignition, sustained activity, broadcasting, access, and report-related activity must be coded as separable claims rather than one undifferentiated signature.

claim_scope.target: The transition by which a represented content becomes consciously accessible.
claim_scope.level: Large-scale cortical dynamics, long-range connectivity, and cognitive access.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That every late frontoparietal response is conscious ignition, that report is constitutive of consciousness, or a full explanation of qualitative character.

basis: Masking, threshold, electrophysiology, imaging, and computational studies report nonlinear and widespread activity associated with conscious access.
The theory makes differentiable predictions about ignition, sustained representation, and inter-areal communication.
limitations: Report, attention, task relevance, and confidence can contribute to canonical late signatures.
The 2025 adversarial collaboration found results compatible with some predictions while challenging offset ignition and parts of the proposed prefrontal representation profile.
evidence_profile.independence: The appended Cogitate Consortium study was designed by proponents and theory-neutral researchers and preregistered divergent predictions; it does not deliver a binary verdict on GNWT.

open_questions: Which ignition signatures survive no-report and task-irrelevant designs?
How should GNWT distinguish conscious broadcasting from attention, decision, memory, and motor preparation?
Which anatomical commitments belong to current GNWT rather than earlier versions?

citation_additions.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness

profiles.scope: Versioned constitutive theory identifying experience with a maximally irreducible intrinsic cause-effect structure.
profiles.boundary_note: IIT 3.0 and IIT 4.0 use materially different formal objects and must be versioned. PCI, neural complexity, differentiation, and ordinary information integration are not direct computations of a full IIT Φ-structure.

claim_scope.target: The intrinsic physical conditions and structure proposed to be identical with phenomenal existence.
claim_scope.level: Phenomenological axioms, causal formalism, and constitutive physical postulates.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That tractable brain-complexity proxies compute IIT quantities, that high functional integration is sufficient, or that the full formalism has been validated in realistic brains.

basis: IIT supplies explicit versioned axioms, postulates, formal definitions, and worked model systems.
Perturbational and complexity findings motivate integration-and-differentiation research but generally test auxiliary or proxy claims rather than full IIT structures.
limitations: Full calculations are intractable for realistic systems and depend on contested choices of substrate, grain, and maximal complex.
The 2025 adversarial collaboration supported some selected predictions while challenging sustained posterior synchronization; it did not test or refute the entire IIT 4.0 formalism.
evidence_profile.independence: The defining formal papers are self-expositions. COGITATE used preregistered predictions jointly specified by proponents and theory-neutral researchers, reducing but not eliminating auxiliary-assumption and interpretation problems.

open_questions: Which feasible observation uniquely discriminates IIT 4.0 from recurrent, workspace, or generic complexity accounts?
How can causal structures be estimated without substituting an invalid proxy for Φ?
How should failed prediction components update a versioned theory rather than generate a binary verdict?

profiles.scope: Higher-order representation account of when first-order mental states are conscious.
profiles.boundary_note: Occurrent HOT theory is one higher-order position. It must remain distinct from dispositional HOT, inner-sense, higher-order global-state, and higher-order state-space accounts.

claim_scope.target: What makes a first-order mental state conscious rather than unconscious.
claim_scope.level: Representational and metacognitive architecture, with proposed neural implementations.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That accurate introspection is required, that higher-order representation must be linguistically structured, or that prefrontal activity uniquely realizes a HOT.

basis: Metacognitive dissociations, confidence manipulations, and some prefrontal findings motivate a role for higher-order representation.
The account offers explicit explanations of misrepresentation and apparently empty higher-order states.
limitations: Metacognitive performance is not equivalent to phenomenal consciousness and may rely on post-perceptual processes.
First-order, recurrent, and global-access theories can explain portions of the same evidence.
evidence_profile.independence: One retained empirical review is coauthored by central proponents; adversarial tests require theory-neutral operationalizations of higher-order representation.

open_questions: What representational relation is minimally sufficient for a HOT?
Can higher-order representation be measured without using report or confidence as a proxy for consciousness?
How should the theory handle conscious states in infants, animals, and impaired metacognition?

profiles.scope: Perceptual-consciousness theory combining intermediate-level representational content with attention.
profiles.boundary_note: AIR is specifically an attended intermediate-level representation account. It should not be generalized into the claim that any attended representation is conscious or that consciousness is identical to attention.

claim_scope.target: The representational level and attentional condition associated with perceptual experience.
claim_scope.level: Perceptual representation, attention, and cognitive neuroscience.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A theory of all conscious thought, that attention and awareness never dissociate, or a uniquely identified neural locus.

basis: Intermediate visual representations plausibly preserve viewpoint-sensitive detail while supporting stable object-level contents.
Attention strongly modulates perceptual visibility and intermediate visual processing.
limitations: Evidence for attention without awareness and awareness under reduced attention challenges a simple constitutive requirement.
Intermediate-level content and attentional selection are difficult to operationalize independently.
evidence_profile.independence: The primary monograph states the theory; the retained comparative review places it within a broader contested theory family.

open_questions: Which level of a perceptual hierarchy is genuinely intermediate across modalities?
What kind of attention is constitutive rather than enabling or report-related?
Can AIR explain nonperceptual experience and contentless states?

profiles.scope: Internal-model account of awareness attribution and the control of attention.
profiles.boundary_note: AST explains why systems model and report awareness through a simplified model of attention. Whether that exhausts phenomenal consciousness is a further philosophical and empirical claim.

claim_scope.target: Awareness attribution to self and others and model-based control of attention.
claim_scope.level: Cognitive, computational, social-cognitive, and proposed temporoparietal neural mechanisms.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That attention itself is consciousness, that awareness reports are always accurate, or that an attention schema resolves phenomenal character.

basis: Social attribution, attentional control, body-schema analogies, and modeling work motivate a simplified internal description of attention.
The theory generates intervention predictions linking disruption of the schema to altered awareness attribution and control.
limitations: Empirical findings often support component functions without uniquely demonstrating an attention schema.
The account risks explaining beliefs and reports about awareness while leaving experience itself underdetermined.
evidence_profile.independence: Both retained defining sources are authored by principal proponents; independent preregistered tests remain comparatively limited.

open_questions: What neural or computational signature distinguishes an attention schema from ordinary metacognitive modeling?
Can nonverbal organisms possess the proposed schema?
Which perturbations selectively alter awareness modeling without simply impairing attention?

profiles.scope: Constitutive role of embodied skill and lawful action-dependent sensory change in perceptual experience.
profiles.boundary_note: Sensorimotor contingency theory is primarily a theory of perceptual experience. Mastery, exercise of mastery, bodily dependence, and the status of internal simulation vary across formulations.

claim_scope.target: Why perceptual experience has modality-specific and world-presenting character.
claim_scope.level: Embodied skill, perception-action dynamics, and philosophy of perception.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That online movement is required for every experience, that neural activity is irrelevant, or an account of all conscious thought and affect.

basis: Active perception, sensory substitution, adaptation, and action-dependent changes support a constitutive or enabling role for sensorimotor structure.
The framework explains modality-specific qualities through distinct laws of sensorimotor dependence.
limitations: Dreams, imagery, paralysis, and passive experience challenge strong online-action readings.
Behavioral mastery may not by itself distinguish conscious from sophisticated unconscious control.
evidence_profile.independence: The primary formulation and authoritative embodied-cognition review support the family while documenting substantial internal variation.

open_questions: Is actual exercise, counterfactual availability, or learned mastery of a contingency required?
How are sensorimotor laws represented or enacted in dreams and imagery?
What differentiates conscious mastery from nonconscious skilled control?

profiles.scope: Reentrant thalamocortical integration and differentiation as a rapidly changing neural substrate of experience.
profiles.boundary_note: Dynamic Core theory historically precedes IIT. Shared language about integration and differentiation does not make its reentrant functional-cluster proposal mathematically or metaphysically identical to later IIT formulations.

claim_scope.target: Neural organization associated with unified and differentiated conscious scenes.
claim_scope.level: Thalamocortical systems, reentrant dynamics, and large-scale functional clustering.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A validated scalar consciousness measure, identity with IIT, or why integrated neural dynamics have phenomenal character.

basis: Conscious states depend on both differentiated repertoires and integration across distributed thalamocortical systems.
Reentrant and effective-connectivity findings motivate transient functional coalitions rather than a fixed anatomical center.
limitations: Integration and differentiation are operationalized in many nonequivalent ways.
Similar dynamics can occur outside consciousness, and direct tests of a uniquely bounded dynamic core are limited.
evidence_profile.independence: The defining source is by a principal architect; the retained scoping review independently identifies the model but does not validate its mechanism.

open_questions: How should a dynamic core be delimited in space and time?
Which measures distinguish conscious reentry from unconscious recurrent coordination?
Which predictions remain unique after separating the theory from IIT?

profiles.scope: Subcortical and affective foundations proposed to generate a basic form of conscious feeling.
profiles.boundary_note: The proposal prioritizes affective consciousness and upper-brainstem organization. It should not be conflated with the claim that cortex is unnecessary for every conscious content or with clinical affect-awareness constructs.

claim_scope.target: The minimal neurobiological basis of sentience and felt affect.
claim_scope.level: Upper brainstem, subcortical affective systems, homeostasis, and neuropsychoanalysis.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That all cortical contributions are merely cognitive, that decorticate behavior proves human-like experience, or the content of every conscious state.

basis: Brainstem damage, arousal systems, affective circuitry, and preserved motivated behavior motivate a subcortical contribution to sentience.
Homeostatic and valence-centered formulations connect consciousness with organismic need and action.
limitations: Arousal, motivated behavior, and affective processing do not independently demonstrate phenomenal experience.
Clinical lesions rarely isolate the proposed generators, and cortical-subcortical interactions are extensive.
evidence_profile.independence: Both retained sources are theory-developing works by proponents; independent discriminating tests against cortical and distributed accounts remain needed.

open_questions: Which subcortical mechanisms are sufficient for valenced experience rather than arousal or action readiness?
How can basic affective consciousness be assessed without report?
How do cortical contents become bound to the proposed affective subject?

profiles.scope: Family of consciousness proposals using hierarchical generative models, prediction error, precision, and counterfactual control.
profiles.boundary_note: Generic predictive processing is not itself a single consciousness theory. Precision, model depth, temporal thickness, counterfactual richness, and global availability are distinct consciousness-specific extensions that require separate attribution.

claim_scope.target: How generative inference may shape conscious content, presence, and access.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That prediction-error minimization is sufficient for consciousness, that all predictive-processing formulations agree, or a unique phenomenal marker.

basis: Perceptual inference, expectation, precision, and hierarchical feedback robustly influence reported experience.
The framework supplies formal tools for modeling hypotheses about content and conscious access.
limitations: Predictive-processing explanations are highly flexible and often fit both conscious and unconscious inference.
Different proposals assign incompatible consciousness-making roles to precision, errors, representations, or action.
evidence_profile.independence: The retained papers explicitly distinguish a broad predictive framework from a mature, singular theory of consciousness.

open_questions: Which predictive quantity changes specifically with consciousness rather than perception or attention?
What observation would falsify a consciousness-specific predictive account?
How should competing precision-, depth-, and counterfactual-based variants be compared?

profiles.scope: Predictive regulation of bodily signals as a basis for emotion, embodied selfhood, and felt presence.
profiles.boundary_note: Interoceptive inference is a framework for embodied self and affect. Broader claims about all phenomenal consciousness must not be inferred from evidence about interoception alone.

claim_scope.target: How generative models of internal bodily causes contribute to feeling and embodied selfhood.
claim_scope.level: Interoceptive, computational, autonomic, affective, and self-representational.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That interoception is necessary for every conscious content, that predictive regulation uniquely explains subjectivity, or that physiological accuracy equals awareness.

basis: Interoceptive manipulations, autonomic predictions, emotion research, and body-ownership phenomena support model-based bodily inference.
The framework links perception and action through homeostatic and allostatic regulation.
limitations: Interoceptive task performance has contested reliability and may not measure awareness directly.
The same observations can support constructionist, appraisal, predictive, or lower-level physiological accounts.
evidence_profile.independence: The retained sources are closely related primary formulations, so independent model comparison remains especially important.

open_questions: Which interoceptive representations are conscious and which remain regulatory?
How are bodily predictions related to phenomenal ownership and first-person perspective?
Can causal manipulations distinguish interoceptive inference from rival emotion frameworks?

profiles.scope: Formal active-inference implementation of workspace ignition and conscious visual access.
profiles.boundary_note: PGNW is a specific computational synthesis. It neither establishes equivalence between active inference and GNWT nor licenses transferring empirical support between the parent frameworks.

claim_scope.target: How ignition, expectation, and precision may jointly determine conscious visual access.
claim_scope.level: Hierarchical Bayesian computation and global-workspace architecture.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: That the simulation uniquely implements GNWT, that variational inference is conscious, or that the model covers affective and nonvisual experience.

basis: The model formalizes qualitative ignition and expectation effects in a generative architecture.
It produces manipulable predictions relating prior expectation and precision to access.
limitations: Simulation success does not show that the brain uses the same representation or optimization process.
The model inherits unsettled operational assumptions from both GNWT and active inference.
evidence_profile.independence: The retained locators identify the same primary paper rather than independent empirical validation; the evidence base therefore remains model-proposer dependent.

open_questions: Which predictions differ from ordinary Bayesian perception without a workspace?
Can model parameters be identified from neural and behavioral data?
How should PGNW be updated in light of empirical challenges to canonical GNWT signatures?

profiles.scope: Explanandum concerning what-it-is-like character, distinguished from access, report, and behavioral function.
profiles.boundary_note: Phenomenal consciousness is a contested construct, not one theory. Using it does not commit the catalog to irreducible qualia, phenomenal overflow, or a particular metaphysics.

claim_scope.target: The experiential character of mental states.
claim_scope.level: Phenomenological and philosophical construct used across empirical and metaphysical debates.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A measurement method, a neural mechanism, metaphysical nonphysicality, or that phenomenal and access consciousness dissociate.

basis: First-person reports and philosophical analysis motivate distinguishing experience from availability and performance.
The construct organizes empirical disputes about report, overflow, and unconscious processing.
limitations: Its extension depends on contested judgments about absent report, marginal cases, and what counts as experience.
Behavioral and neural evidence requires bridging assumptions that can import a favored theory.
evidence_profile.independence: The retained primary and authoritative sources define and contextualize the construct; they do not provide an independent detector of phenomenality.

open_questions: Can phenomenal consciousness be operationalized without collapsing it into access or report?
What evidence could discriminate phenomenal overflow from rich unconscious representation?
How should the construct extend to nonhuman and artificial systems?

profiles.scope: Availability of information for reasoning, flexible control, and report, contrasted with phenomenal character.
profiles.boundary_note: Access consciousness is a functional construct, not automatically a global-workspace mechanism. Availability, actual access, reportability, working memory, and executive control must remain analytically distinct.

claim_scope.target: The functional availability of represented information to multiple cognitive systems.
claim_scope.level: Cognitive architecture, reasoning, action control, and report.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Phenomenal character, one neural implementation, a sharp access threshold, or equivalence with verbal report.

basis: Reasoning, flexible behavior, working memory, and report paradigms provide operational access measures.
The distinction clarifies which theory predictions concern functional availability rather than experience.
limitations: Most access measures combine perception, attention, memory, decision, metacognition, and motor response.
A system may be poised for use without exercising or externally revealing that capacity.
evidence_profile.independence: The primary source introduces the distinction; the retained review compares its use across consciousness theories.

open_questions: Which consumer systems and counterfactual uses are required for access?
Is access graded, multidimensional, or governed by a discrete transition?
Can access be measured in nonverbal systems without circular behavioral assumptions?

profiles.scope: Conceptual and empirical separation of selective prioritization from conscious awareness.
profiles.boundary_note: Attention and awareness each name heterogeneous families. Apparent dissociations depend on how attention, awareness, performance, and residual processing are operationalized.

claim_scope.target: Whether and how attentional selection differs from conscious experience and access.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: Complete independence, that attention is never necessary, or that one paradigm directly measures awareness without selection.

basis: Dual-task, masking, cueing, inattentional-blindness, and no-report paradigms show partial behavioral and neural dissociations.
The distinction prevents attentional enhancement from being treated automatically as an NCC.
limitations: Residual attention is difficult to exclude and awareness measures commonly require attention and decision.
Different studies contrast distinct forms of spatial, feature-based, endogenous, or exogenous attention.
evidence_profile.independence: The retained sources establish the conceptual landscape but do not settle the strength or direction of every dissociation.

open_questions: Which kinds of attention are necessary for which kinds of awareness?
How can awareness be measured without introducing attentional and report demands?
Do attention and awareness have separable causal neural signatures across modalities?

profiles.scope: Phenomenal, representational, spatial, temporal, and subject unity as distinct explanatory targets.
profiles.boundary_note: Unity is a family of explananda. Evidence for integration, synchrony, or one behavioral controller does not by itself establish phenomenal unity or a single conscious subject.

claim_scope.target: The respects in which simultaneous and temporally extended experiences belong together for a subject.
claim_scope.level: Phenomenological, representational, metaphysical, cognitive, and systems-neural.
claim_scope.does_not_establish: A single neural binder, an indivisible Cartesian subject, or that all conscious contents are mutually accessible.

basis: Ordinary experience, binding phenomena, multisensory integration, temporal continuity, and split-brain cases motivate separable unity questions.
Competing theories make different predictions about integration, access, and subject-level organization.
limitations: Behavioral coordination and neural integration are indirect evidence for phenomenal co-consciousness.
Split-brain, neglect, dissociation, and local processing do not yield a simple count of conscious subjects.
evidence_profile.independence: The authoritative source distinguishes multiple unity problems; the theory review shows that proposed neural solutions are not interchangeable.

open_questions: Which unity relations are necessary for a single conscious field?
How should subject unity be inferred in split or partially disconnected systems?
Can unity be graded without collapsing into generic connectivity?
